items.title: 1 arrested, another wanted for attempted murder following reported parking dispute stabbing in Mississauga: police
items.summary: One person has been arrested and charged, while another remains at-large following a double stabbing in Mississauga on Saturday night. The incident, which investigators initially described as an altercation with a “possible stabbing,” happened at a shopping plaza in the Cooksville neighbourhood near Dundas Street West and Parkerhill Road, just west of Hurontario Street. m. officers responded to a call for a disturbance in a parking lot. “Upon arrival, officers located two adult men suffering from stab wounds following a reported parking dispute,” they said in a news release. ” Police said officers at the scene searched the area and quickly located one of the suspects without incident. Ali Halimi, 30, of Mississauga, was arrested and charged with assault. The charge has not been tested in court. A second male suspect, whom police believe stabbed the victims and is in possession of the knife, remains outstanding. He is wanted for attempted murder.

Upon arrival, officers located two adult men suffering from stab wounds following a reported parking dispute. Both victims were transported to hospital with serious injuries and are now in stable condition. Officers searched the area and quickly located one of the suspects without incident. Ali Halimi, a 30‑year‑old man from Mississauga, was arrested and charged with Assault. items.title: Stabbing: 2 men sent to hospital in Mississauga, one man arrested
items.summary: Two men were seriously injured in a stabbing in Mississauga Saturday evening, police say. m. following reports of an altercation and possible stabbing. Police later confirmed in a social media post that two men had been stabbed. Both were taken to hospital with serious injuries. Updates on their conditions are unknown. Additional information about the victims, including their ages, places of residence, and whether they were known to the suspects, has not been released. Investigators say a man was taken into custody, while police continued to search the area for a possible second suspect. Police have not shared details about the altercation that led to the stabbing. The public was asked to avoid the area as the investigation continued. items.title: Mississauga Pesäpallo Players Set Sights on World Cup in Sydney This October
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, a Mississauga-based community group is hoping to eventually bring the Pesäpallo World Cup to the city after building a growing following for Finland's national sport locally. The outlet reports a group of Greater Toronto Area residents, some travelling from as far as Oakville and Burlington, regularly gather at Bloor Athletic Field in Mississauga to play the sport. Mississauga.com describes pesäpallo as a fast-paced game resembling baseball, featuring a distinctive field, unusual running patterns and near-constant action that appeals to players of different ages, backgrounds and skill levels. According to the outlet, while some participants treat it purely as a recreational activity, others are preparing to represent Team Canada at the 12th Pesäpallo World Cup in Sydney, Australia, running October 2 to 5 this year. Mississauga.com reports the four-day tournament is being organized by the Finnish Society of Sydney and is expected to draw teams from Australia, Finland, Canada, Germany and India competing in men's, women's and mixed categories.

items.title: Cooksville Plaza Stabbing Leaves Two in Hospital, One Suspect in Custody
items.summary: According to CTV News, two people were taken to hospital following an altercation with what police called a possible stabbing at a shopping plaza in Mississauga's Cooksville neighbourhood late Saturday afternoon. The outlet reports the incident happened near Dundas Street West and Parkerhill Road, just west of Hurontario Street. CTV News reports police said the two people suffered serious but non-life-threatening injuries and were taken to separate hospitals, with one sent to a trauma centre. According to the outlet, paramedics described the injuries differently, saying one patient had life-threatening injuries and the other had serious, life-threatening injuries. CTV News reports investigators took one suspect into custody while continuing to work out whether any other suspects remain outstanding. The outlet reports a large police presence remained in the area, with officers advising people to avoid the vicinity.

items.title: SaiGon Pho and Grill Opens Second GTA Location Inside Square One's Food District
items.summary: According to INsauga, Toronto-based Vietnamese restaurant SaiGon Pho and Grill has opened a second location inside The Food District at Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga. The outlet reports the restaurant serves traditional Vietnamese dishes including slow-simmered pho, grilled pork rice, vermicelli bowls, banh mi sandwiches, spring rolls and grilled meats. INsauga reports the chain's first location opened near Finch Station in Toronto in 2025. According to the outlet, the new Square One location features a dine-in space finished with wood accents and soft lighting. INsauga reports the opening is part of a wave of new restaurants that arrived in Mississauga and the wider region in August, as diners look for new options heading into the fall.

items.title: After Nearly a Decade, Heart Lake's Harbourside Fish and Chips Serves Its Last Order
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga and Brampton lost several longtime restaurants in August, with two closures the outlet highlighted in detail. The outlet reports Harbourside Fish and Chips in Brampton's Heart Lake neighbourhood has closed after nearly a decade in business, having been opened in 2017 by Dean and Helen McCormick. INsauga reports the restaurant served traditional fish and chips alongside shrimp, crab cakes, scallops, poutines and deep-fried desserts, and had previously been ranked among the city's top fish and chips shops. According to the outlet, the restaurant announced its closure on Instagram, thanking the Heart Lake community for its support over the years. INsauga also reports a fair trade, vegan cafe operating as a social enterprise at 2520 Eglinton Avenue West in Mississauga is closing that location after 12 years. The outlet reports the cafe said it will continue its community programming elsewhere in Mississauga, including initiatives focused on youth leadership, climate action, art and job skills.
